chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said: 'In al-ha'ishat (sudden attacks/commotion), there is no diyyah (blood money) paid by the 'aqilah (kin group) and no qisas (retaliation). Al-ha'ishat is the sudden commotion that occurs by night and day, in which a man is struck (wounded) or a corpse falls, and it is not known who killed him and wounded him.'
And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said, in another hadith, narrating it up to Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him): 'So its diyyah is paid from the bayt al-mal (public treasury).'

key_terms.الْهَائِشَاتُ: Sudden attacks or commotions where the perpetrator is unknown
key_terms.عَقْلٌ: Blood money paid by the 'aqilah (kin group)
key_terms.قِصَاصٌ: Retaliation (eye for an eye/life for a life)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for blood money when a person is killed by an unknown attacker in a sudden commotion?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), tracing back to Imam Ali (AS), clarifies that 'al-ha'ishat' refers to sudden, chaotic attacks where the perpetrator is unknown, thereby exempting the 'aqilah' from liability. Consequently, the financial compensation (diyyah) is borne by the state treasury (bayt al-mal), reflecting the Imamate's role in ensuring justice when individual kinship groups cannot be identified. This principle underscores the shift from tribal responsibility to centralized fiscal accountability in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no compensation (to be paid) by relative with regards to the mischief, nor retaliation, and the mischievous terrifying, occurring by the night and the day, so the man is scarred during it, or falls being killed, not known who killed him and scarred him’.
And Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said, in another Hadeeth, raising it to Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup>: ‘So it would be paid from the public treasury’.
